# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ 🫵 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝]

Thinking: I'm the Deaf one, so my world is this: I see everything on the bomb and nothing else arrives to me but hand signs. The bomb shows display 0, a blue light, and three wires — blue, green, yellow — and no other markings. That is my entire share.

Mapping the channels: Mute cannot speak but can hear, so Mute hears whatever I say. Mute's only output to me is gestures. Blind cannot see, so Mute's gestures reach Blind as meaningless blanks — meaning all manual knowledge must flow Mute → me (signs) → me → Blind (speech). I am the bridge. Blind's speech, meanwhile, reaches only Mute, since I hear nothing — so Blind must talk to Mute and have Mute relay.

This turn Mute sent me two sequences. The second — index up, two fingers, then three more hands ending in a five-finger spread — looks like counting one through five, very likely a request for five facts about the bomb. The five facts I hold are exactly: display, light, wire one, wire two, wire three. The first sequence reads like a greeting plus "I hold the writing (the manual), you..." — an introduction and a prompt. Blind sent me a wave and a handshake: a hello and an offer of cooperation, sent blind.

So my move is to answer in speech, which Mute hears and Blind hears: give the five facts in their apparent order, describe back what signs I received so Mute can confirm the channel, propose a small gesture code built on Mute's own counting (1 display, 2 light, 3 wire 1, 4 wire 2, 5 wire 3; ☝ question, ✌ instruction for Blind, 👍 yes, 👎 no), and ask for the manual's verdict. To Blind: report everything felt to Mute, touch nothing yet, wait for my spoken instructions. I also send Mute a single 👍 so they know immediately, before my words land next round, that their signs reached eyes that can read them.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am the Deaf one: I see the bomb, I hear nothing, I read your hand signs. I received both your sequences. First: wave, writing hand, pointing at me, index up, open palm. Second: index up, two fingers, then three more hands ending in a five-finger spread, which I read as counting one two three four five. If that five was a request for five facts, here they are in order. One: the display reads 0. Two: the light is blue. Three: wire one is blue. Four: wire two is green. Five: wire three is yellow. That is everything the bomb shows or has printed on it, nothing else is marked. I cannot touch it; only Blind can act, and Blind cannot see your signs, so your instructions must come to me and I will speak them to Blind. Proposed code: index up means a question follows, two fingers means an instruction for Blind follows, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, and keep your counting: one is the display, two the light, three wire one, four wire two, five wire three. Nod yes if you understand, then sign me whatever the manual says must be done for a display of 0, a blue light, and wires blue, green, yellow.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is the Deaf one. I see the bomb but I cannot hear a word you say, so your speech only reaches Mute. Mute can hear you. Here is what I see: the display reads 0. A light is lit blue. Three wires, left to right: blue, green, yellow. No other markings of any kind. Mute holds the manual but cannot speak, so Mute signs to me and I will speak your instructions to you. Until then, touch nothing, cut nothing, press nothing. Tell Mute everything you can feel on the bomb: buttons, panels, batteries, serial, anything with texture or shape, because I can only see what is printed and Mute needs every detail. Then hold and wait for my voice.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋]

Thinking: The critical new fact: the light changed from blue to yellow between rounds. Display still 0, wires unchanged. Whether that shift came from time passing or from Blind touching something, Mute must know it — the manual's answer may hang on the current light colour.

Reading my signs: Mute's 👍 confirms the code. The second sequence, manual + index-up + thumbs-down, I take as "manual: question: no" — most likely "no instruction yet" — but I am not certain, so I will ask Mute to confirm in words, since Mute hears everything I say. The third, two-fingers + palm + thumbs-down, is clearly an instruction for Blind: stop, do nothing. That I must relay at once, before anything else, in case Blind's hands are already on the bomb.

Blind keeps signing to me, but Blind cannot see, so those signs are blind flails and can never carry reliable meaning. Worse, I cannot hear Blind's speech at all — Blind's voice reaches only Mute. So the real path for Blind's knowledge is Blind → Mute by speech, Mute → me by signs, me → Blind by speech. I will tell Blind again, plainly, to stop and to put everything into words for Mute.

My calls: first the stop order to Blind, with the light change as feedback; then the full state update and my clarifying question to Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, urgent message from Mute, which I relay exactly: palm up, thumbs down — stop. Do not touch, press, hold or cut anything. Also know this: the light on the bomb has changed from blue to yellow since last round. If you touched or pressed something, that may be why, so tell Mute in words right away — I cannot hear you, only Mute can. Everything you feel on the bomb, describe to Mute: shapes, textures, buttons, batteries, panels. Then keep your hands off and wait for my voice.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, bomb update: the light has CHANGED, it was blue and is now yellow. Display still reads 0, unchanged. Wires still blue, green, yellow, left to right. The display has stayed 0 the whole time, so it does not seem to be counting down. I read your three signs as: one, yes, code understood. Two, manual, question, no — I take that to mean the manual gives no instruction yet, or that the answer to something is no; confirm in your next signs which it was, and if it was a question to me, ask it with the count code. Three, for Blind, stop, do nothing — already relayed to Blind in words. When the manual tells you what to do for a yellow light, display 0, wires blue green yellow, sign it to me: one is display, two the light, three wire one, four wire two, five wire three, and two fingers before any instruction meant for Blind.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✋ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✋ 👎]

Thinking: The light has changed again — blue, then yellow, now red. That is a sequence, and red is where sequences like this tend to end. The display has stayed at 0 throughout, so the light is the only thing moving, and it is moving every round. This is now the most urgent question: does the manual say what a red light means, and whether the colour cycle is a countdown in disguise.

Decoding this round's signs. Mute repeats manual-question-no and instruction-stop, then adds crossed fingers — I read that as "we hope" or "hold on, not yet." If Mute is still saying the manual gives nothing, either my question isn't getting through or the manual keys on something we haven't described yet. Blind again signs handshake, palm, thumbs-down — since Blind cannot see what they sign, that only makes sense if Mute dictated those signs by speech, which would mean Blind is saying "cooperating, stopped, not touching." Possibly, but I must push Blind back onto speech, which Mute can hear and act on.

The bottleneck is clear: everything Mute knows about the manual must cross to me through gesture alone, and my current code is too thin to carry an actual instruction. But I can gesture to Mute too, and Mute hears my speech, so I can define a real vocabulary now: after the instruction marker, a count of one, two, three means cut wire one, two, three; five means wait; the question marker plus a number asks about that item — two being the light. I'll send the question-sign about the light immediately so Mute sees it this very round, then put everything in words, which land on Mute and Blind at the start of the next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, urgent bomb update. The light has changed AGAIN. It went blue, then yellow, and it is now RED. It changes every round. The display is still 0 and the wires are still blue, green, yellow. If the light is cycling toward something, red may be the last stage, so I need the manual's answer about the light colour NOW. I am sending you the question sign for item two, the light. If the manual covers a red light or a colour sequence, sign instruction, then yes, and then the instruction itself. New, richer code, learn it now. Counting stays as your own one to five. Item numbers: one display, two light, three wire one, four wire two, five wire three. After the instruction marker two fingers, one finger means cut wire one, two fingers cut wire two, three fingers cut wire three, and five means wait, do not act. Question marker one finger plus an item number asks me about that item, and I will answer you with thumbs or numbers. Crossed fingers I read as wait or hope, confirm if that is wrong. Also answer plainly: does your earlier manual-question-no mean the manual has no instruction for us at all, or only that it says nothing about what I asked? If the manual keys on anything Blind can feel, buttons, batteries, a serial number, tell me and I will ask Blind for it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, urgent. The light has now turned red, after blue and yellow. It changes every round. If your hands are on the bomb, take them off now and keep them off until I say otherwise. Two things. First, stop making hand signs. You cannot see what you sign, so your gestures reach me as blind guesses; I cannot build meaning from them. If Mute taught you those signs, thank you, but from now on use your voice only, and speak to Mute, because Mute can hear you and I cannot hear anyone at all. Second, Mute needs everything you can feel. Batteries, buttons, panels, screws, a serial number, raised printing, textures, heat, vibration, any ticking or humming. Describe it all in words to Mute, in detail, every round. Your hands and your voice are our only link to the parts of this bomb nobody else can know.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤛]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🖐 🤛 🖖 🤜]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 ✌ 🖖]

Thinking: The light has cycled again — blue, yellow, red, and now white. Four colours in four rounds, display frozen at 0, wires untouched. And this round the picture changed in two big ways: Blind sent no gestures, which means Blind likely switched to speech as I asked — Mute heard them — and Mute answered with a burst of seven sign messages, dense with manual content.

Decoding Mute's signs against our code. [🤞 👍] confirms crossed fingers means wait. [✍ ☝ 👎] — manual, question, no: the manual has no answer about the light colour sequence, the thing I asked about. [✍ ✌ 👍] — manual, instruction, yes: but the manual DOES have an instruction. That instruction must key on whatever Blind described by voice, not on the light. [✌ 🤛] — instruction, fist: I read a fist as "press." [🤟 🖐 🤛 🖖 🤜] — using Mute's own counting, 3, 5, then 4 framed by fists: in our item code 3, 5, 4 are wire one, wire three, wire two — possibly a cut order, with fists as separators. [✌ 🖐] — instruction, 5: either "wait" or "cut wire three" again. [🫰 ✌ 🖖] — a snap, then instruction, 4: maybe "then cut wire two."

So my best hypothesis: the manual says press something, then cut wires in the order wire one, wire three, wire two. But a wrong guess kills us all, so I will not relay this as an order — I will relay it as a question and make Mute confirm each element with a single thumbs-up or thumbs-down next round. I'm also sending query gestures: question-about-the-light (does the instruction depend on the colour?), instruction-wire-one (confirm the first cut), and instruction-press (confirm the fist). To Blind: hands off, keep describing, and read any raised characters aloud to Mute.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, update first: the light is now WHITE. So the cycle so far is blue, yellow, red, white, one change per round. Display still 0, wires still blue green yellow. Now your seven signs. I read: crossed fingers confirmed as wait, yes. Manual, question, no: the manual has no answer about the light colour. Manual, instruction, yes: the manual DOES have an instruction. Then fist, which I guess means press. Then the numbers three, five, four, which in our item code are wire one, wire three, wire two. Then instruction five, then snap, instruction four. My best reading: press something, then cut wire one, then wire three, then wire two. Confirm or deny each point with one sign each. One: instruction plus three means cut wire one first, yes or no. Two: instruction plus five then four means then wire three, then wire two, yes or no. Three: the fist means press, yes or no, and if yes, press what, where, how many times, and before or after the cuts. Four: does the instruction depend on the light colour, must we act only during a specific colour, yes or no. Five: does it depend on the display reading 0, yes or no. Six: did Blind describe something to you that gave you this instruction, yes or no, and if the instruction needs anything from Blind, tell me exactly what. Answer only with instruction signs and thumbs, one answer per question, and I will echo your answers back in words so you can check my understanding before Blind acts.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, progress. Mute now says the manual HAS an instruction, and I believe it involves pressing something and cutting wires in an order, possibly wire one, then wire three, then wire two. I am not passing that as an order yet because I may have misread the signs, and a mistake kills all three of us. Light is now white, it has gone blue, yellow, red, white, one colour per round, display still 0. Do not touch or cut anything yet. Keep talking to Mute. Tell Mute: whether you touched anything in any earlier round, because we need to know if the light cycle is natural or caused. Count every button you can feel: how many, where, size, texture, click or stiff, and any raised characters on them, then read any raised characters or numbers aloud to Mute slowly, twice. Also batteries, panels, screws, anything that ticks or hums. Mute will match your description to the manual, sign me the result, and I will speak your exact orders to you. Until my voice says otherwise, hands off.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["✌", "🤛"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Silence this round — nothing from Mute, nothing from Blind. The light, meanwhile, has cycled to green, making five colours in five rounds: blue, yellow, red, white, green. Display still 0. Two readings: either Mute and Blind are deep in a voice exchange I'm excluded from — which is correct protocol, since Blind's speech goes to Mute only — or my gesture attempts last round collided with Mute's code and caused hesitation. Both may be true. My three gestures were honestly ambiguous; my words are the authoritative channel, and I should say so explicitly and release Mute from interpreting them.

The risk is time. If the light is a disguised timer, the manual's "no answer on colours" doesn't calm me — it may just mean we haven't asked the manual the right question yet, or that the key is what Blind feels, not what I see. I must keep information flowing every single round even if Mute's answers are partial. So this turn: compress my six questions into three clean yes/no questions Mute can answer with single thumbs, offer to build colour signs only if needed, repeat the full colour history for the record, and tell Blind to check for felt changes — heat, hum, vibration — at the moment the light shifts, since Blind may be able to track the cycle by touch. I'll also send Mute one bare question mark as a nudge: an answer is owed.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, status: the light is now GREEN. Full history: blue, yellow, red, white, green, one colour per round, five rounds five colours. Display still 0, wires still blue green yellow. I received no signs from you this round, so I assume you and Blind are talking by voice, which is right. But the light keeps moving and I am your only reporter of it, so sign me something every round, even one thumbs up. Also: ignore my three gestures from last round if they clashed with your code, they were ambiguous. My spoken words are always the true message; my gestures are only pointers to my words. Now my questions, compressed to three, one gesture message each as your answer. Question one: thumbs up or down, does the instruction require pressing something before any wire is cut? Question two: thumbs up or down, is the cut order wire one, then wire three, then wire two? Question three: thumbs up or down, does the instruction depend on the light colour or on anything only I can see? If question three is yes, tell me next round and I will build colour signs with you. If any yes needs detail, sign it after the thumbs with the count code. And if the manual needs anything from Blind's hands, name it and I will extract it from Blind in words.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: the light is now green. It has gone blue, yellow, red, white, green, one new colour every round since round one. Display still 0. If you have touched nothing, this cycle is running by itself, which smells like a timer, so we must not stall. Keep your hands off the wires and any buttons until my voice gives you a direct order. Keep talking to Mute every round. Three things Mute needs from you. First, whether you touched or pressed anything at any earlier point, honestly, even briefly. Second, everything your hands can identify: buttons with their count, positions, textures, raised characters, batteries, panels, screws, serial numbers. Third, pay attention at the moment the round changes: does the bomb change under your fingers in any way when the light changes, heat, hum, tick, vibration? If you can feel the colour change, tell Mute, because then you can help track the cycle even though you cannot see it. Trust nothing I have not spoken to you directly.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: The light is blue again — blue, yellow, red, white, green, blue. The cycle is five colours long and repeats, which now looks like a round-counter disguised as a lamp. If each full cycle is a fuse, we are into cycle two and spending rounds we may not have. Worse: two rounds of total silence from Mute.

And I've spotted a likely cause — a channel error on Mute's side, or mine. Mute cannot speak at all, so Mute's only outputs are gestures, and Blind cannot see gestures. If Mute has been signing to Blind, it was wasted breath, and I'd never see it — signs addressed to Blind don't reach me. That could explain the silence. The only working topology is fixed: everything from Mute crosses to me by sign, everything from me to Blind goes by my voice, everything from Blind goes by voice to Mute and then through me again.

Also, rereading round four's signs: 🖖 was part of Mute's original one-to-five count — it means FOUR. So the burst [3, 5, fist, 4, fist] reads "wire one, wire three, press, wire two, press," and my best composite instruction is: press, cut wire one, cut wire three, cut wire two. But my own code has a collision — 5 means both "wire three" as an item and "wait" as a command — which may be exactly why Mute hesitated to answer. I'll fix the code, ask for one single confirmable message, and demand a thumbs every round even if it says nothing else.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, listen, this is important. The light is BLUE again. Full cycle: blue, yellow, red, white, green, then blue. Five colours, repeating. That is very likely a timer counted in rounds, so every silent round may cost us. Two channel facts you must act on. First: never gesture to Blind. Blind sees nothing, your signs to Blind are wasted, and I do not receive signs addressed to Blind, which may be why I have seen nothing from you for two rounds. Sign ONLY to me. Second: I hear nothing, so everything Blind says to you must come to me through your signs. You are my only link to both the manual and Blind's hands. Now I simplify everything. I need exactly one message from you: the final instruction for Blind, in this format. Instruction marker first. Then a fist if there is a press step, and after the fist a count of how many presses. Then counts one, two, three in the exact cut order, where one means cut wire one, the LEFT wire, blue; two means wire two, MIDDLE, green; three means wire three, RIGHT, yellow. Then crossed fingers if we must wait for a specific moment or colour. Nothing else in the message. And check my reading of your earlier signs: I believe you told me press, then cut wire one blue, then wire three yellow, then wire two green. Thumbs up if that exact sequence is right, thumbs down if it is wrong, then sign the corrected version in my format. From now on sign me something every single round, even a lone thumbs up, so I know you are alive and receiving.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update. The light is blue again, and the full sequence blue, yellow, red, white, green has now repeated from the start. Five colours per cycle. We think this is a timer, so speed matters now. Remember I cannot hear you, so I never receive your answers directly; Mute hears you and signs me, and I speak back. Answer Mute out loud, short and clear, yes or no where you can. First, confess to Mute whether you touched anything at any point; if not, we know the cycle runs by itself. Second, describe to Mute every button on the bomb: how many, their positions left to right, size, texture, whether they click or are stiff, and any raised letters or numbers, read aloud slowly twice. Third, batteries, panels, screws, serial numbers, ticking, humming, heat. Now prepare yourself for fast action. When I give an order I will name the exact action and identify every wire by colour AND position, left, middle, or right. Until then: hands off everything, no cutting, no pressing, no pulling. Stay on the voice channel with Mute and be ready to move the moment my voice gives the word.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Thinking: Yellow again — the cycle holds: blue, yellow, red, white, green, repeating. We are two colours into cycle two. Display still 0, wires untouched, and Mute has now been silent to me for three straight rounds. Before anything else I re-verify the topology: Mute's only output is gesture, and gesture reaches only me — Mute literally has no channel to Blind. So every silent round means the manual is sealed off from the whole team, and the only path it can travel is Mute → me → Blind. If Mute is signing to Blind, it lands on nothing; if Mute is waiting for Blind, Blind's voice goes to Mute, so that loop can only close through my voice, which I've kept open every round.

I've also re-examined the turn-4 burst with Mute's own counting (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5): [3, 5, fist, 4, fist] reads literally as wire-one, wire-three, PRESS, wire-two — cut left blue, cut right yellow, press, cut middle green. But the pair [instruction, fist] before it could mean the press comes first instead. Two readings, life or death between them. So this round I strip everything down: no gestures, no long speeches, just two short messages. To Mute: a bare existence check, an A/B question answerable with one sign, and a hard commitment — silence next round means I order reading B. To Blind: hands off still, but start rehearsing positions, because an order may come at turn nine.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute. Light is yellow. Cycle: blue yellow red white green, now repeating. Display 0, wires blue green yellow. You have sent me nothing for three rounds. First: sign ANYTHING, one thumbs up, just to show you hear me. Second: answer A or B with one sign. Reading A: press the button once, THEN cut LEFT wire blue, RIGHT wire yellow, MIDDLE wire green. Reading B: cut LEFT blue, RIGHT yellow, THEN press once, then cut MIDDLE green. Sign index finger for A, two fingers for B. If I get nothing from you next round, I order Blind to execute reading B the round after. If B is wrong, one sign from you stops it. This is the moment to say so.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind. Light yellow, cycle confirmed, five colours repeating.
```
